section.title: Wrex Tells It Straight
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: The brief names the form outright: a memorial, six speakers on their feet, the eulogy's swing between a laugh, an angry line, and a stretch that can barely be got through. Jack is a deliberate exception to strict alternation and to normal voice balance - she opens and closes by the brief's fixed order, so she holds two of the seven turns while Tali, Grunt, Liara, Joker and Wrex each hold one. Her two turns are sized as ordinary single turns rather than doubled, but together they total roughly twice any other voice's word count, which is the "two turns' worth" the brief asks for. Section targets were raised after the voice checkpoint, at the user's instruction to let the speeches run to their natural length rather than be trimmed to a grid; the middle five now sit at 900-1050 and the episode target at 6650. Each middle turn answers the one directly before it; Jack's closing turn answers the whole room, not just Wrex. Grunt's bible is new and unused before this run - he is built distinct from Wrex throughout: Wrex remembers the Rebellions and the genophage firsthand, Grunt states krogan history as Okeer's tank taught it and then flattens it to "put in me, not lived," and his own lived material is small and recent (the Rite, the Citadel, the mess hall, the war) and used in full. The "gets a detail wrong and is corrected" requirement is carried by two beats, not one: Grunt states the assumed version (died on his feet with a gun) and Joker mis-hears whose voice was on the channel, and Wrex corrects both flatly before giving the room the true version - shot on the way to the landing zone, then killed driving a vehicle into a banshee to clear passage for Hammer. Wrex reads that off the wreckage he found days later, not off memory; nobody in the room watched Thomas die, and each of them holds only a piece. No section narrates the Crucible's mechanism or Shepard as confirmed dead; Thomas's Synthesis sympathies, where they surface, are framed as a political stance he held in life, never as knowledge of the ending.

required_facts.fact: To seal the turian-krogan alliance, the Urdnot leader (Wrex or Wreav) demands the genophage be cured. Once Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks has stabilised Eve and prepared the cure, Shepard leads a joint turian-krogan strike on Tuchanka to disperse it through the Shroud, the atmospheric tower above the krogan homeworld. Before the operation, Dalatrass Linron privately offers Shepard a deal: the salarians will back the war effort if Shepard lets Mordin secretly sabotage the cure, keeping the krogan weakened. Shepard can accept, refuse, or tell the krogan leader. The krogan convoy drives for the Shroud but is halted when Kalros, the largest known thresher maw, is roused in the catacombs beneath an abandoned krogan city and destroys a bridge. A Reaper Destroyer guards the Shroud. Eve proposes activating the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros against the Reaper while the cure is completed. Shepard activates the hammers; Kalros drags the Destroyer down. The Shroud is left damaged and unstable, and the cure must be released manually from the top of the collapsing tower. The outcome is choice-conditional. If Shepard preserved Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2 (per `mordin_loyalty`) and did not accept the sabotage, Eve survives the procedure and the krogan gain a healthy future. If Maelon's data was destroyed, Eve dies of complications regardless. If Mordin is alive and the cure is genuine, he insists on going up the tower himself and is killed when it detonates, singing as he dies; if the cure is sabotaged and Mordin realises, Shepard can shoot him, or he goes up to fix it and dies anyway. If Padok Wiks replaced Mordin, Wiks dies in the tower. A sabotaged cure can also be carried out with the krogan none the wiser, especially under Wreav (per `genophage`: cured, or secretly sabotaged). Whatever happens, the Reaper guarding the Shroud is destroyed and the krogan commit forces to the war; a genuine cure earns their full strength, while sabotage risks later exposure.
The Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud is dragged down and killed by the thresher maw Kalros
Per `genophage`: the genophage is genuinely cured, or secretly sabotaged by Mordin at the Dalatrass's request
Per `mordin_loyalty`: Eve survives the cure if Maelon's data was preserved, otherwise she dies of complications

The salarian scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks if Mordin is dead) is usually killed in the collapsing Shroud tower completing the cure; Mordin can instead be shot by Shepard if he insists on fixing a sabotage
The Shroud tower is destroyed
The krogan join the war against the Reapers; a true cure yields full krogan support, sabotage risks a later rebellion
Per `krogan_leader`: under Wrex the krogan become steadfast allies; under Wreav they are more belligerent
If cured and Wrex lives, Eve later carries Wrex's children and helps rebuild krogan society

In the climactic endgame of Mass Effect 3, as Reaper forces ravaged Earth and the Crucible—an ancient superweapon built by the Protheans—required activation at the Citadel, Commander Shepard and Admiral David Anderson led a massive galactic assault on London, England. The Reapers had constructed a towering conduit—a massive structure built from organic and metallic components—in the war-torn city. This conduit, built according to mass relay principles but modified by Reaper technology, served as a direct transport mechanism connecting the ground of Earth to the Citadel, which had been mysteriously repositioned above the planet. The conduit functioned unlike standard mass relays: it emitted a constant, brilliant beam of blue light into the sky, continuously transporting matter (primarily the dead and dismembered remains of slaughtered populations) directly from Earth's surface to the Citadel. The structure had no visible element zero core and, critically, allowed living organic matter to survive transit—arriving at ballistic but survivable speeds—rather than disintegrating as with conventional relays. The Reapers appeared to have multiple destination termini on the Citadel, as different individuals arrived at separate points on the station. The assault ran in two ground stages. First Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" with M-920 Cain rounds so the Hammer ground force could land; the team then regrouped at a Forward Operating Base where Shepard held final words with surviving allies before Anderson gave the battle plan. The second stage pushed through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles coordinated with EDI on the Normandy destroyed a Reaper Destroyer blocking the road to the conduit. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final charge. The galactic assault on the conduit was devastating. Allied forces from across the galaxy—humans, turians, asari, salarians, quarians, krogan, and others— launched a coordinated ground assault to penetrate the structure and secure access to the Citadel. However, Harbinger, the Reaper flagship and commander of the local Reaper forces, personally defended the conduit with overwhelming firepower, killing or maiming most of the allied assault force. The majority of the attacking soldiers were annihilated, their bodies adding to the biomass flowing through the conduit itself. Despite the horrific casualties, Commander Shepard and Admiral Anderson managed to fight their way through the structure and reached its heart. Anderson, wounded but resolute, helped push Shepard toward the conduit's exit point. Shepard survived the ascent through the conduit and materialized on the Citadel, while Anderson arrived at a slightly different point on the station. Upon reaching the Citadel, Shepard gained access to the Crucible's control mechanisms and the Catalyst—the artificial intelligence that had guided the Reaper cycle for countless eons. At this critical juncture, Shepard was confronted with a series of final choices that would determine the fate of the galaxy: to Destroy all synthetic life (eliminating the Reapers and the geth but also killing EDI), to Control the Reapers (uploading Shepard's consciousness to command them), to achieve Synthesis (merging organic and synthetic life), or to Refuse the Catalyst's offer (allowing the cycle to continue unchanged). The consequences of this choice—affecting the survival of the geth, EDI, the Reapers themselves, and organic civilization—would echo across the galaxy for generations.
Most of the galactic assault force on Earth is killed or maimed; the conduit's light beam carries thousands of casualties toward the Citadel.
Harbinger's personal defense of the conduit results in massive casualties among the allied ground forces.
Commander Shepard reaches the Citadel and gains access to the Crucible control mechanisms and the Catalyst.
Admiral David Anderson reaches the Citadel (severely wounded) and assists Shepard in reaching the Crucible.

Per the final choice (Destroy/Control/Synthesis/Refusal): - Destroy: All Reapers are destroyed along with the entire geth species and EDI; synthetic life is eradicated; the cycle of extinction theoretically ends. - Control: Shepard's consciousness is uploaded into and merges with the Reaper collective, giving Shepard godlike power but ultimately disembodying them; the Reapers are brought under Shepard's control. - Synthesis: Shepard's genetic code is merged with all organic and synthetic life in the galaxy, creating a new form of hybrid existence; the Reapers are transformed into custodians of this new synthesis. - Refusal: The Catalyst and Reapers are allowed to proceed with the cycle; the Crucible fails and the Reapers continue the harvest; galactic extinction continues indefinitely.
Shepard's ultimate fate is determined by the choice made and the Crucible's firing.

If Destroy or Control are chosen and sufficient War Assets are gathered, Shepard survives (though potentially as a Reaper in Control ending or as a hybrid in Synthesis); otherwise Shepard dies in the Crucible's activation.
Depending on the ending, Anderson either survives (on the Citadel) or dies from wounds sustained during the assault.
The galaxy's future is fundamentally altered: either the Reapers are destroyed (ending the cycle), controlled by Shepard, synthetically merged with organics, or allowed to continue their harvest.
If Destroy is chosen, the geth and EDI are killed along with the Reapers; if Control or Synthesis is chosen, they survive and are transformed.

Per the Extended Cut: epilogue scenes show Admiral Hackett ordering the fleets to evacuate Earth's orbit, the Normandy caught in the energy wave in transit and crash-landing on a garden world, the Charon Relay's core breaking up while the relay itself survives and the mass relay network is later repaired, and a Liara time-capsule message. A fourth outcome, Refusal (declining to activate the Crucible or shooting the Catalyst), dooms the current cycle to the Reaper harvest but leaves records that let a later cycle break the pattern, shown in an alternate Stargazer scene. Shepard's name is added to the Normandy memorial wall beside Anderson's unless a high-strength Destroy leaves Shepard's survival ambiguous.

scenes.title: The Party at Shepard's Apartment
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station
scenes.where: Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden

beats.text: Joker suggests the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy. Shepard buys Party Provisions from the kiosk at the bar on the second floor of the Silver Coast Casino for 100 credits, then sends the invitations from the private terminal in the apartment office.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Absences nobody explains: Gardner, Allers, Chakwas, Chambers, Adams, Donnelly and Daniels are all missing. Traynor mentions in the kitchen that Chakwas is dealing with a medical emergency on the Citadel. The rest are simply not addressed.
Glyph asks the Commander what kind of party this is — quiet or energetic — and the answer sets the opening conversations. The groupings themselves are set by the guest list, not the theme.

Opening arrangement: Liara and Traynor in the kitchen with Tali, Samara and Garrus. EDI and Joker at the bar by the window with Miranda and Jacob. James and Cortez on the couches by the piano with the Virmire survivor and Jack. Wrex and Grunt upstairs on the balcony with Zaeed and Javik. Kasumi flits between the bar and the kitchen, uncloaking to interject.

Wrex and Grunt spend the opening trading krogan insults over who is stronger — Grunt calling Wrex a fossil and belittling his age. If the mood is energetic they headbutt each other to settle it and Shepard has to stop them before the furniture goes.
Grunt tells Wrex that two of Aralakh Company's recruits had opposed his appointment, and that only one of them had to be dealt with, the other having been killed in a fight.

Garrus's verdict on the place is that it would be a good place to retire, its sightlines appealing to his sniper sensibilities. He complains at a quiet party about the lack of hard drinks and at an energetic one dares Shepard to try the swill on offer.

Traynor cannot get over the size of the apartment — the electric bill alone would have covered her college tuition. Tali's version is that the same bill would have bought her an air conditioner for her suit, which she does not have, and it gets hot in there.
The group toasts the Normandy. Traynor admits she still feels like an outsider next to people who have histories with Shepard, and everyone weighs in.

Traynor gets everyone recounting how they met Shepard. Tali's memory is that all she could think about was hoping Shepard had showered, because her filter needed replacing and humans carry a lot of germs. Liara notes that three years on she is drinking Shepard's booze through a straw, and calls that progress.

Second phase, energetic: Liara and James argue on the balcony about whether biotics or muscle wins, with Jacob, Miranda, Jack, Kaidan and the Virmire survivor taking sides. James shows off his "fine example of peak physical form"; Liara says she is going to challenge him to a pull-up contest, which gives him pause. When James jabs at "flawed implants," Kaidan shoots back with how hard he has worked and his resulting ability to Reave, drawing trepidation from Liara and Jacob. Shepard picks a side. If Shepard backs biotics, Liara lifts him off the floor with no visible effort and Kasumi uncloaks to goad him into sit-ups; if Shepard backs muscle, the push-ups happen instead and Kaidan is flabbergasted, though Shepard can comfort him by saying that his kind of physical excellence is Shepard's kind too.

Second phase, energetic, at the bar: Joker gets ganged up on by Cortez, Garrus, Wrex and Javik or Zaeed over refusing to keep a sidearm in the cockpit. Garrus's line is that a weapon he cannot get to is no weapon at all. Wrex offers Tuchanka as the harshest planet alive and dares anyone present to last a day there, says krogan parties involve a lot of violent deaths, and announces he needs to shoot something. If Shepard keeps the mood up and backs the shooting practice, he makes good on it — bottles on the counter, with Javik and Zaeed joining in.

Second phase, energetic, at the door: Grunt works the vid-phone as bouncer, distinguishing fake salarian lip-hair from the real thing and establishing that Shepard has no half-brother named Sheppy the Volus. He is briefly tempted by cookies and turns them away anyway.

Second phase, quiet: Grunt dares Wrex into a drinking contest and will not accept his excuses, goading him with "logic is for salarians" and the observation that the great Urdnot Wrex has backed down from a challenge. Elsewhere Liara and James compare the SSV Normandy with the SR-2 in the den, with Tali acting out both ships' handling and engine noise and reporting that the SR-2 is harder to perform. Garrus and Zaeed stand on the balcony discussing how to make the apartment defensible. Kaidan, Joker and Samantha discuss EDI on the second floor.
Traynor and Joker — or Traynor and EDI, extremely awkwardly — work through Traynor's recorded opinion of EDI's voice, while Tali nearly poisons herself with cheese trying to change the subject.

Third phase, quiet: Tali ends up on the floor of the downstairs bathroom, wasted and barely comprehensible, having got an omni-tattoo at Jack's suggestion. Shepard tells her to get some rest and hears fragments of her muttering while passing the door afterwards. Grunt is wherever the food or the drink is, announcing his hunger. Liara and James play cards in the den with Javik and a cloaked Kasumi, Glyph dealing if Shepard sends it there.

Third phase, energetic: Grunt is wasted under the running shower upstairs, muttering about being a Space Cowboy, asking whether someone is a wizard, mourning that hanar cannot wear sweaters and reporting that he found a blue rock for Liara. Downstairs the dancing starts between the kitchen and the conference room — Traynor, Cortez, Jack, Samara, Garrus and Tali — with Glyph setting up the floor if sent. Kasumi is in the downstairs bedroom closet going through Shepard's underwear drawer.

Garrus on watching Shepard dance: record it and broadcast it at the Reapers, because they will either run, melt down, or fall in love. Someone starts reciting the periodic table; at "element 69" the humans snicker and Garrus reminds them it is thulium.

Garrus's quiet-party alternative is micro-filaments — tiny explosives laid in a grid across the glass by the door that shred anyone coming through — coordinated with Zaeed over comms, and he later gets to name a booby-trapped coffee maker "caffeine rush".

At the end Shepard assembles everyone by the couch for a group photo. Couples face each other; everyone else looks at the camera. The photograph hangs afterwards by the downstairs bar, opposite the fireplace.

evidence.text:
Priority: Tuchanka followed Priority: Sur'Kesh and required completion of either Tuchanka: Turian Platoon or Attican Traverse: Krogan Team. Eve was the key to curing the genophage, but the cure had to be synthesized and dispersed across Tuchanka from the Shroud, a salarian-built atmospheric tower later used by the turians to spread the original genophage. The salarian STG scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks) would travel to the Shroud with Eve.

At Tuchanka the Reapers were using the Shroud to poison the atmosphere, and a Reaper Destroyer guarded the site. The krogan attacked from the ground with turian air support. Dalatrass Linron privately told Shepard that the Shroud had been sabotaged to prevent a cure, offering salarian war support if Shepard let the krogan believe a fake cure had been deployed. Shepard could reveal or conceal this deal at several points.

Shepard's team defended Eve against husks at the sacred Hollows, where Eve rallied the assembled clans; if Wrex led, tension rose with his disloyal brother Wreav. The krogan convoy set out for the Shroud but was halted by a damaged road, forcing Shepard's squad through ancient catacombs of a krogan city abandoned for millennia, where artifacts depicted Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, and a rachni-like corpse hinted at events at Utukku. After fights against Cannibals, Ravagers, Brutes and Marauders, Wreav's (or Jorgal Thurak's) truck was dragged under by Kalros. Eve proposed using the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros to distract the Reaper. Shepard activated both hammers while dodging the Reaper Destroyer's laser and legs and fighting continuously spawning Brutes; Kalros then dragged the Reaper beneath the surface.

At the damaged Shroud, if Maelon's data had not been saved Eve had died. Mordin (or Wiks) prepared to disperse the cure. Shepard could let him complete it—deploying a counter-sabotage and the real cure, killing Mordin in the explosion—or sabotage it per the Dalatrass. If Wrex and Eve were both dead and the deal unrevealed, Mordin could be persuaded to fake his death and live; otherwise curing the genophage cost him his life. The turians and krogan joined as war assets; sabotage instead granted the Salarian First Fleet. If the cure was faked and Wrex led, he later discovered the deception and died confronting Shepard.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure at the Shroud on Tuchanka

evidence.text: It is revealed that some krogan females managed to survive Maelon's experiments. STG led a mission to capture the females and brought them to Sur'Kesh. If Mordin survived the Suicide Mission, he would leak the existence of the females to the Urdnot clan leader, provoking the proper political pressure to force the salarian dalatrass to release them. However, only one female, nicknamed Eve, survived, and Cerberus is looking to preserve the genophage to prevent an alliance between turians and krogan. If Maelon's research was preserved, it would be adequate to complete a cure, which would be released on Tuchanka through the Shroud facility. Dalatrass Linron, fearing that the krogan would expand again if the genophage is cured and the Reapers defeated, as well as seek revenge on the salarians and turians for unleashing it in the first place, then reveals to Shepard that the salarian STG team had previously sabotaged the Shroud to prevent cure dispersal and offers the salarians' support if the Commander hides the sabotage. Mordin later overrides the sabotage and sacrifices himself in order to release the genophage cure to all krogan, therefore ending the genophage for good and allowing the krogan to join Shepard's alliance to save Earth from the Reapers. If Shepard had hidden the sabotage up until Mordin has to take the elevator up to the top of the Shroud tower, Mordin notes some odd readings from which he'll deduce that the shroud is sabotaged if Shepard doesn't reveal it to him first. Shepard will then have a choice to either let Mordin dispense the cure or shoot him in order to prevent him from releasing the cure. Mordin will still go up the elevator if he's shot but will be unable to make it to the console thus leading the cure to fail. If Urdnot Wreav is clan leader and Eve is dead, it is possible for Shepard to convince Mordin not to release the genophage cure. Mordin will then pretend that he was killed while administrating the cure, and will go to the Crucible to help in its construction. If Mordin didn't survive the Suicide Mission, his role in curing the genophage will be filled by Padok Wiks. If Shepard chooses to use the Crucible for the synthesis of organic and synthetic life, the genophage is cured regardless of whether Mordin or Padok released a cure on Tuchanka.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure at the Shroud on Tuchanka

evidence.text:
The Shroud was a salarian construct on the surface of Tuchanka, built roughly 2,000 years ago to stabilize the planet's atmosphere after the krogan's self-induced nuclear winter. It was originally deployed by a series of ground-based mass-driver towers that launched its components into orbit; all but one of those towers were later destroyed, and that surviving tower came to be called "the Shroud," though the name was technically inaccurate. The tower was repurposed to disperse particles and chemicals into Tuchanka's atmosphere for climate control.

The Shroud was part of a salarian scheme to uplift the krogan during the Rachni Wars, when a losing Council traded technology to the krogan in exchange for soldiers. During the subsequent Krogan Rebellions, after the genophage was released, a salarian STG team sabotaged the Shroud to ensure that any genophage cure could not be easily disseminated through it. The structure stood in an old arena built as a shrine to Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, placed there in the hope that the threat would deter anyone from reaching the Shroud and discovering the sabotage.

In Mass Effect 3, Commander Shepard and Mordin Solus (or Padok Wiks) needed the Shroud to disperse a genophage cure across Tuchanka as part of securing a turian-krogan alliance. A Destroyer-class Reaper had seized the tower to poison the atmosphere. Shepard's squad dodged its beam to reach two maw hammers that summoned Kalros, who attacked the Destroyer; the Reaper smashed her into the Shroud, damaging it, but Kalros dragged the Reaper underground. Shepard then reached the control room, where a temperature malfunction and the STG countermeasures made remote bypass impossible, forcing the salarian scientist to access the controls manually. Whether or not the cure was distributed, the Shroud was ultimately destroyed in an explosion.

evidence.text: Eventually, the salarian doctor declares Eve ready for travel to Tuchanka. After the genophage cure is prepared, Shepard arrives on Tuchanka and the krogan prepare to use the Shroud to spread the cure. A confrontation ensues at the Hollows, the sacred burial ground of the krogan, when some of the krogan clans became hostile on seeing a salarian involved in the operation. The potential fight is averted when Eve delivers a speech that they must put aside their differences and fight together against the Reapers. In a joint operation with the turians to attack a Destroyer guarding the Shroud, the krogan led by Clan Urdnot leave the camp in Tomkahs. However, the operation goes wrong as the krogan get off to a late start, and the turians end up with a solitary airstrike where they are outmatched. The convoy then comes under attack and Shepard orders them to move out and leave the squad behind. After Shepard manages to fight through the ruins and back to the convoy, Eve proposes an idea to eliminate the Reaper. She mentions that the Shroud is near the two largest Maw Hammers in existence, and they can summon Kalros, "The Mother of all Thresher Maws". Eve says that Tuchanka is as much her home as it is the krogans', so if the hammers are activated, then she will come. While the maw has the Reaper distracted, the salarian scientist can finish the cure. As Shepard sets off, Eve heads into a nearby lab with her salarian doctor to finish the cure. If the Commander saved Maelon's data, then Eve survives the procedure to cure the genophage, and Shepard later gains strong support from the krogan clans. At the conclusion of the mission, Eve finally reveals her birth name to the Commander and says that they will always be friends. She later sends a message to Shepard, informing the Commander of the various krogan clans gathering in the Kelphic Valley, to whom she promises to speak to ensure that genophage cure isn't taken for granted. If Shepard chose to destroy Maelon's data back in 2185, however, Eve dies due to complications from having incomplete data, regardless of whether Shepard sabotaged the genophage cure or not. This causes several krogan clans to fall into conflict over who was responsible for Eve's death, weakening them as a whole. The krogan hold a funeral for her, attended by many krogan, the Urdnot leader, as well as Shepard. Her body is brought to the center of the Hollows, incinerated in a funeral pyre. Eve's eulogy is given by the current Urdnot shaman. Even if the genophage is dealt with, Eve may still die later, if Shepard does not aid Lieutenant Victus in disarming a rearmed turian bomb left over from the Krogan Rebellions. Eve was rallying the clans in the Kelphic Valley when the bomb explodes, obliterating her and the krogan population present. Shepard shortly receives a message from the Urdnot leader stating she died.

evidence.text: An STG facility on Sur'Kesh conducts research on the genophage, in addition to finding possible applications for uplifting varren, vorcha, and yahg. Following former agent Maelon Heplorn's efforts on curing the genophage, the STG traveled to Tuchanka, retrieved the krogan females who were subjected to Maelon's experiments, and brought them to this facility. The Urdnot leader, through sources within STG, eventually hears of this and tasks Shepard with returning the females to Tuchanka. While the sole surviving female, Eve, is being transported through the facility, Cerberus forces attack the base, having been fed information by STG agents who oppose the development of a cure. Shepard successfully extracts Eve and leaves the salarians to clean up after remaining hostiles. After the Krogan Rebellions, STG sabotaged the Shroud on Tuchanka in order to prevent any potential genophage cures from being disseminated by the structure. Unfortunately Shepard needs the structure for that purpose, in order to secure the krogan's support for the Reaper war. The sabotage can be fixed by the STG agent or former agent (Padok Wiks or Mordin Solus) responsible for completing the cure, or if not, allow the sabotage to go unfixed and let the krogan believe they received the real cure. Depending on Shepard's previous actions, various STG elements can join the war effort against the Reapers.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure at the Shroud on Tuchanka

evidence.text: The decision to involve the krogan in proceedings causes major problems; the asari pull out of the summit altogether, believing turian\-krogan relations too fragile for anything to be accomplished. A diplomatic meeting is held between Shepard, Primarch Victus, Dalatrass Linron, the leader of the Salarian Union, and the clan chief of the krogan, either Urdnot Wrex or his brother and successor Wreav. The dalatrass is openly hostile and insulting to the krogan leader, who is ambivalent to the plight of the turians, insisting that the Reapers are moving on Tuchanka and refuses to provide military assistance unless their own demand is met; that a cure is created for the genophage. The dalatrass flatly refuses to agree to such a demand, arguing that what Shepard and Victus are planning to do in curing the genophage is the same rash mistake the salarians made when they uplifted the krogan to fight against the rachni, while Victus believe the plan impossible because it would take years they don't have to synthesize a cure. However, the Urdnot leader reveals intel he has received that following the experiments of a salarian scientist into curing the genophage on infertile krogan females, an STG team rounded up the survivors of the experiments\- a group of now fertile females who are also immune to the genophage\- and took them offworld. The dalatrass, under pressure, reluctantly reveals that the females are being held at an STG base on Sur'Kesh and accedes to their release, though she insists that curing the genophage will have dire consequences for her people and the galaxy as a whole. Shepard, their squad and the krogan leader arrive on Sur'Kesh to oversee the exchange, meeting up with the salarian scientist in charge: Mordin Solus, if he survived the suicide mission, or Padok Wiks, if Mordin died. This scientist is responsible for the krogan females' care and is revealed to be the source who leaked information on their existence to the krogan. However, as a side effect of the cure, the females suffered from weakened immune systems and only one has survived. A Cerberus strike force hits the base shortly during the exchange, seeking to kill the surviving female and stop any hope of a cure for the genophage. Shepard and their squad are forced to fight off Cerberus troopers deploying into the base as the salarian scientist and the Urdnot leader attempt to extract her. The team escape Sur'Kesh with the female krogan, who is christened 'Eve' by the salarian scientist, and the cure is rapidly developed. Eve takes some time to regain her strength, and when she's ready the salarian doctor proclaims her fit for travel to Tuchanka, where she's needed for the last leg of the genophage cure's completion. The krogan and turian leaders approach Shepard with problems of their own, requesting that the Commander deal with them if there's time. The Normandy then deploys to Tuchanka when Shepard decides it is time, where the Reapers have begun attacking in force. They decide to release the cure from the Shroud, an enormous salarian structure built to repair Tuchanka's atmosphere that was secretly repurposed to spread the original genophage. En route, Shepard is contacted privately by Dalatrass Linron, who insists Shepard cannot go through with the genophage cure and reveals that the Special Tasks Group sabotaged the Shroud years ago to prevent it being used for such a plan. The dalatrass offers Shepard a deal; prevent repairs to the Shroud, thus causing the cure to fail, and in exchange, the salarians will provide military support and technical expertise to help construct the Crucible. Upon arrival on the planet, the Urdnot leader rallies the krogan forces, who will work with a turian fighter squadron to distract a Reaper destroyer using the Shroud to further poison the atmosphere of Tuchanka. However, the plan almost immediately goes awry, with the krogan ground forces delayed and the fighters decimated as they attempt to attack without support. The ground forces are scattered and Shepard's team is forced to detour through ancient and impressive krogan ruins, that also happens to be home to the largest known thresher maw. They improvise a new plan, luring the thresher maw into attacking the Reaper destroyer to buy them time. This strategy is significantly more effective than the last: despite overwhelming Reaper opposition, Mordin/Wiks and Shepard make it to the Shroud and Kalros manages to kill the destroyer. Eve is either alive in a safe place or dead depending on whether Shepard saved Maelon's data months before but the cure is fully completed nonetheless and awaiting planetwide dispersal. There are, however, complications.

evidence.text:
The genophage was a biological weapon deployed against the krogan by the turians during the Krogan Rebellions to sharply reduce krogan numbers through an introduced genetic mutation. Rather than reducing female fertility, it reduced the probability of viable pregnancies: most fetuses never developed nervous systems and many krogan died in stillbirth. Every cell in a krogan was infected to prevent gene therapy from countering it. The weapon was developed by the salarians, who intended it as an undeployed deterrent, believing its consequences too terrible to use; the turians, favoring "massive retaliation," deployed it immediately upon completion. Krogan numbers dwindled rapidly, fertile females became prizes of war, and the warlord Shiagur used her fertility to attract the strongest males to her army. After centuries, awareness of impending extinction bred a dangerous fatalism among the krogan. There was no known cure; some krogan invested in companies such as Binary Helix, and a black-market trade in krogan testicles arose from the unsubstantiated belief that transplants could counteract the effects.

In Mass Effect, Saren Arterius developed a genophage cure, possibly aided by Binary Helix or Sovereign, and used it to breed a krogan army on Virmire. Shepard and Captain Kirrahe destroyed the facility and the cure with a nuclear weapon, potentially causing a rift with Wrex. In Mass Effect 2, Mordin Solus explained that the krogan had been evolving resistance, so he and STG colleagues engineered a new genophage variant to hold population growth at pre-industrial levels. Mordin's loyalty mission revealed his former student Maelon, kidnapped by Blood Pack krogan on Tuchanka, working on a cure amid dead test subjects (including humans and a female krogan); Maelon claimed to work willingly and feel no guilt. Shepard could destroy or keep his data.

In Mass Effect 3, STG recovered surviving krogan females and brought them to Sur'Kesh, where only "Eve" survived. Cerberus sought to preserve the genophage to prevent a krogan-turian alliance. With Maelon's research, a cure could be dispersed through the Shroud facility on Tuchanka. Dalatrass Linron revealed STG had sabotaged the Shroud and offered salarian support if Shepard concealed this. Mordin (or Padok Wiks if Mordin died) overrode the sabotage and sacrificed himself to release the cure. If Shepard hid the sabotage, they could let Mordin proceed or shoot him to make the cure fail; if Wreav led and Eve was dead, Mordin could be talked out of it and fake his death. A Citadel Archives document dated 710 CE showed turians activating the Shroud over the objection of a lone salarian who called it genocide. In Mass Effect: Andromeda, krogan colonists departed still afflicted but with a natural resistance mutation, bolstered by gene therapy during cryosleep, raising offspring survival from 0.1% to 4%.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure at the Shroud on Tuchanka

evidence.text:
The Urdnot Camp was a small, rubble-strewn settlement on the krogan homeworld of Tuchanka, controlled by Clan Urdnot. A shuttle landing pad connected to the camp proper by a derelict passageway. The camp contained the throne dais of Clan Urdnot's leader, a building housing the Urdnot shaman where representatives of other clans gathered, a varren-fighting pit, the clan's food stores (frequently raided by invasive pyjak), a merchant's kiosk run by Ratch, and the laboratory of the clan's Lord High Researcher, Fortack.

In 2185 Commander Shepard traveled to the Urdnot Camp to aid Mordin Solus in searching for a missing fellow Special Tasks Group member during the mission "Mordin: Old Blood," and to help Grunt complete his Rite of Passage in "Grunt: Rite of Passage." Shepard could also speak with the leader of Clan Urdnot, who was either Urdnot Wrex (if he survived Virmire and joined Shepard) or Urdnot Wreav. Additional activities included helping a krogan mechanic find a combustion manifold to repair a vehicle, addressing the clan's chronic pyjak infestation, and betting on a varren fight. If Urdnot Wrex was alive, a Clan Nakmor representative was present at the camp to negotiate an alliance with Clan Urdnot, and Shepard could interact with the negotiation. The traditionalist Gatatog Uvenk was also present, opposing the current clan leadership. evidence.text: Clan Urdnot was a krogan tribe on Tuchanka. Urdnot Wrex, a mercenary from the clan, crossed paths with Commander Shepard during the hunt for Saren Arterius and could join the squad. By 2185 Shepard visited a clan base camp while helping the tank-bred krogan Grunt. If Wrex led the clan, Urdnot was a reformist group holding neutral ground open to all krogan, requiring each clan to punish its own criminals, while clans expelled from the neutral ground were slaughtered by Wrex's allies; Wrex had also stopped weapon manufacture and ordered his chief researcher Fortack to study crop genetics and medicine. Completing Mordin Solus's loyalty mission strengthened the clan; under Wrex the survivors of Clan Weyrloc were absorbed, while under Wreav their weapon stocks were plundered. By 2186 Clan Urdnot had become the uncontested representative of krogan power to the galaxy, having absorbed or destroyed Clans Nakmor, Jurdon, Quash, and the ferocious Clan Raik. During the Reaper invasion the clan leader met Dalatrass Linron and Primarch Adrien Victus at a war summit aboard the Normandy SR-2, where turian aid depended on krogan help, krogan help on a genophage cure, and the salarians refused the cure; Shepard secured access to a STG base on Sur'Kesh holding a fertile female krogan called Eve. During the mission to deploy the cure through the Shroud on Tuchanka, the krogan leaders met at the Hollows, where Eve urged them to unite against the Reapers. Depending on Shepard's choices a real or fake cure was dispersed, and the clan leader pledged to aid the turians on Palaven. If Wrex led, he intended to rebuild krogan civilisation and restrain clans seeking revenge; if Wreav led, he pursued an aggressive path, having commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any krogan in known history. More traditional than Wrex, Wreav prized his own clan over the krogan race as a whole and preferred war to peace, summed up in his line, "Tuchanka and the krogan live together in war. The planet hates us, and we hate it."

In Mass Effect 2, Shepard first met Wreav on Tuchanka, where he thanked the Commander for killing his brother, since it made him clan leader. Because he was a traditionalist, rivals like Gatatog Uvenk posed little challenge. He permitted Grunt to join Clan Urdnot after the Rite of Passage, pleased that the resulting hatred would be "influential." In Mass Effect 3, if Wreav was leader he was aggressive and racist toward turians and salarians, treated Eve and female krogan as property, and kept Jorgal Thurak as his second. Liara, via Glyph, revealed that Wreav had commissioned more weapons of mass destruction than any krogan in known history and had used some against other clans, though Urdnot retained a conventional stockpile. His diplomacy relied on the threat of krogan invasion. During the land assault on the Shroud, Wreav's tomkah was sunk by Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, and he was believed dead, to Wrex's indifference: "he was a pain in the ass, anyway."

Once the genophage was cured, Wreav claimed credit, spreading stories of "the day Wreav cured the genophage" to cement his authority. At the final battle on Earth he ordered krogan to cooperate with allied forces while studying their tactics, implying future hostile intent. If Shepard hid the salarian sabotage and Wreav was leader, he never learned the cure was fake and pledged full krogan support, and Shepard also gained the salarian First Fleet. evidence.text: **Ryncol** is an extremely potent liquor created by the krogan. Its exact composition is unknown, but it is clearly a very strong drink, given that it is created by and for the krogan. Grunt comments that ryncol "hits aliens like ground glass." Humans can survive drinking ryncol, although it is apparently unsafe for volus. One obtainable datapad contains a complaint made by a pirate about how the YMIR Mech he purchased "leaks \[fuel] like a volus after a mug of ryncol." When Commander Shepard visits the Dark Star Lounge and asks the bartender for five consecutive drinks, the Commander will be given a glass of ryncol. The bartender jokes that Shepard will "set off radiological alarms" after they drink it. Elcor and quarians can also survive drinking ryncol, although in case of the latter one must take immuno\-supplements and anti\-virals for weeks before attempting even one shot. In quarians it apparently makes them feel like "stained glass", and feels like "sipping knives" during the act itself. However, ancient quarians were capable of imbibing ryncol without issue since their immune systems weren't ruined yet by Migrant Fleet living. Ryncol apparently has "pure" and cocktail variants. It can be sold in 190 proof bottles. The turian bartender in the Dark Star Lounge creates a green ryncol mix served to Shepard by mixing separate components together. As per his prediction, it does indeed knock Shepard out, leading to a short sequence where the Commander groggily wakes up on the floor of the Dark Star's bathroom. In Jack's opinion, Shepard's stash of creme de menthe in the Personal Apartment can sicken people more than a sample of pure ryncol. Ryncol is also highly flammable: while on Silversun Strip, Grunt narrates to Shepard that he in fact used it as a Molotov cocktail merely by throwing a regular bottle at a C\-Sec aircar. Ryncol is highly acidic, capable of melting through machinery. Vomit from ryncol consumption is apparently purplish in color.

evidence.text: The resultant Krogan Rebellions continued for nearly three centuries. The krogan sustained massive casualties, but their incredible birth rate kept their population steadily increasing. They also had no compunction about resorting to extreme tactics, such as using redirected asteroids as weapons, almost rendering several planets uninhabitable. Soon their victory seemed inevitable. In desperation, the Council turned to the recently discovered Turian Hierarchy for aid. The turians unleashed the genophage on the krogan home worlds: a bio\-weapon engineered by the salarians. The genophage caused near\-total infant mortality in the krogan species, with only one birth in every thousand producing live offspring. No longer able to replenish their numbers, the krogan were forced to accept terms of surrender. For their role in quelling the Krogan Rebellions, the turians were rewarded with a seat on the Citadel Council. The krogan, on the other hand, still suffer from the effects of the genophage. Over the last millennium krogan numbers have steadily declined, leaving them a scattered and dying people. Some try bizarre treatments for the genophage, including testicle transplants. But, faced with the certainty of their extinction as a species, most krogan have become individualistic and completely self\-interested. They typically serve as mercenaries for hire to the highest bidder, though many still resent and despise the Citadel races that condemned them to their tragic fate. Wrex comments disdainfully that clubs, bars and brothels often try to hire krogan bouncers, reducing his people to some kind of status symbol.

evidence.text:
Krogan were common soldier enemies seen across the galaxy in the first Mass Effect game, used as shock troops by mercenary bands and pirate groups for their ability to charge, deal heavy weapons fire, and inflict powerful melee attacks. Saren, having found a genophage cure, also bred an army of krogan to supplement his geth, so krogan and geth were usually encountered together in his forces.

In combat these krogan wielded either an assault rifle and shotgun or a sniper rifle and pistol, the latter limited to Inamorda's bodyguards; assault krogan closed in while snipers held back for Assassination shots, and despite rushing they had no true melee attacks. Every krogan enemy regenerated once before dying unless killed in the air or by cold, incendiary, toxic or high-explosive rounds. They were dangerous on all difficulties and especially on Insanity, where most had Immunity and could one-shot the player with melee. Recommended tactics were keeping them airborne or staggered with biotics, Neural Shock or high-force weapons, using rapid-fire toxic damage or Warp to deny regeneration, and in open areas levitating and ejecting them from the map for instant kills.

evidence.text:
The krogan were large reptilian bipeds native to Tuchanka, a harsh world of scarce resources and vicious predators. They thrived there, but as their technology advanced their birth rate exploded and wars over dwindling territory escalated into a global nuclear war roughly four thousand years ago that left Tuchanka a radioactive wasteland and the krogan reduced to primitive warring clans. Two thousand years later the salarians discovered and "uplifted" them, relocating some krogan and giving them technology including the Shroud to stabilize Tuchanka's atmosphere, so that krogan numbers could be thrown against the rachni in the Rachni Wars. The rapidly breeding krogan drove back and eradicated the rachni, were hailed as saviors, granted conquered and Citadel worlds, and honored with the Krogan Monument on the Presidium.

Unchecked by Tuchanka's conditions, the krogan population swelled and they forcibly seized inhabited worlds. When they settled the asari colony Lusia and Overlord Kredak defied the Council, the Krogan Rebellions broke out, lasting nearly three centuries. The krogan used redirected asteroids as weapons; in desperation the Council enlisted the Turian Hierarchy, who deployed the salarian-engineered genophage, causing near-total infant mortality (roughly one viable birth per thousand). The krogan surrendered, the turians gained a Council seat, and krogan numbers steadily declined, leaving a scattered, fatalistic people who mostly worked as mercenaries.

Krogan biology featured redundant organs (two hearts, four lungs, four testicles, hence the slang "quad"), a neuroconductive backup circulatory system making them nearly impossible to paralyze, thick hazard-resistant hides, shoulder humps storing fluids, 240-degree vision, lifespans exceeding a thousand years, and a berserk "blood rage." Culture prized strength, self-reliance and territory; the weak were "not worth killing." Fertile females were prized, lived in separate clans, and were the level-headed counterparts to the males. Rites (Rite of Life, Passage, Honor, Firsts, Union, Authority) were preserved by the nameless clan shaman; the dead were consigned to the Void on funeral pyres or displayed as skulls in the sacred Hollows. Ancient deities included Vaul and Uzin. In 2185 Mordin Solus revealed the krogan were evolving against the genophage and his team applied a modified version. In the 2186 Reaper War, Shepard could cure the genophage at the Shroud (with Eve, Mordin or Padok Wiks) in exchange for krogan aid, or let the salarian sabotage stand; outcomes ranged from krogan repopulation under Urdnot Wrex to Urdnot Wreav being deceived. Separately, Clan Nakmor joined the Andromeda Initiative, later founded New Tuchanka on Elaaden under Overlord Nakmor Morda after a mutiny and a broken Nexus leadership deal.

evidence.text:
The page catalogs beverages consumed across the Mass Effect galaxies, spanning sustenance, personal preference and social lubrication. It lists dozens of named drinks with their species associations, effects and in-game contexts rather than telling a single story.

Alcoholic entries include Akantha, a popular asari liquor with a smoky flavor that cuts hangovers; asari honey mead, brewed in an Ardat-Yakshi monastery and the most expensive liquor in Aria T'Loak's bar; batarian ale, a potent green drink; Serrice Ice Brandy, a 1,000-credit favorite of Dr. Chakwas; turian brandy, which Tali'Zorah drinks through an "emergency induction port" (a straw); Elasa, a Thessian drink nicknamed "Sorrow's Companion" that Anderson drank in Chora's Den during his 2165 divorce; horosk, a hard turian drink strong enough to induce comas; ryncol, an extremely potent krogan liquor; and Noverian Rum, which Aria lamented being unable to obtain. Species-specific intoxicants include the hanar's mindfish (a hallucinogenic skin oil), the angaran marljeh and tavum, the volus bina, and krogan drinks such as burukh, sovak juice (used to name newborns via belching contests) and "liquefied turian," a reverse-chirality dare drink with adverse effects on all who tried it. Methanol is safely ingested by some species and mined by Terminus pirates on Antirumgon.

Cocktails feature heavily, many mixed by Samantha Traynor during Shepard's Citadel party using her college bartending knowledge: the Full Biotic Kick, Quad Kicker, Tasty Tankard, Frozen Pyjak (made from a bartender's spill pad and ice), Perfection, and the Weeping Heart (a martini with mild drell-skin venom). Umi Henon's concoctions in Andromeda, including Combat Juice and an angaran wine and ryncol mix, caused blackouts and wild dancing in Ryder. The Vortex on the Nexus served the Dirty Squirrel, Lucky Leprechaun, Tall Moose and Rotten Scoundrel via bartender Dutch Smith.

Non-alcoholic entries include coffee, credited by SAM for its own existence through Alec Ryder's consumption; soda; and sports drinks Tupari (with an aggressive marketing campaign claiming it revives ancestors) and its rival Paragade. Wine entries cover champagne, Thessia Red (the Illusive Man ordering a "'47"), and various bottles Anderson purchased. Whiskeys named include Mount Milgrom scotch, one 645-year-old bottle of which reached Andromeda and could be stolen by Reyes Vidal from Sloane Kelly's storeroom. Mass Effect: The Official Cocktail Book (2024) collects real-world recipes for many of these drinks.

Being compared to Shiagur was considered a mark of honor: the Urdnot Shaman might bestow the compliment on a female Shepard who understood the krogan better than some of their own kind, and her name was invoked in a song Mordin Solus could sing for Eve.

evidence.text: Due to the brutality of their surroundings, natural selection has played a significant role in the evolution of the krogan. Unlike most sentient species, krogan eyes are wide\-set \- on Earth, this is common among prey animals, and in this case it gives the krogan 240\-degree vision, giving them greater visual acuity and awareness of approaching predators. Krogan eyes have narrow pupils. Their irises may be red, green, amber, or blue in color. Prior to the genophage, krogan could reproduce and mature at an astonishing rate. Females are known to produce clutches of up to 1,000 fertilized eggs over the course of a year. In present conditions, according to EDI, the odds of a krogan successfully giving birth to two females stand at 1 in 2,000, though krogan biology is slowly adapting to the virus. Their large shoulder humps store fluids and nutrients in much the same way as an Earth camel, enabling them to survive extended periods without food or water. In particular they require very little water intake; a 55\-gallon tank system can sustain an entire colony of krogan for over 10 years. A bigger shoulder hump is seen as a sign of high status, showing how successful an individual krogan is at hunting. Their thick hides are virtually impervious to cuts, scrapes or contusions, and they are highly resistant to environmental hazards, including toxins, radiation, and extreme heat and cold. Consequently their diets can include food and drink which would prove very dangerous to other species—a fact reflected in the krogan liquor of choice, ryncol, which is said to "hit aliens like ground glass". Younger krogan have yellow or green markings on their hides. These markings darken to brown or tan over time, showing their age. Younger krogan tend to have looser plates on their head with soft spots in between. When they grow older the plates grow together to form one whole. Krogan typically stand over 7 feet. Heavy creatures, krogan have been known to weigh at least 150 kilos, upwards of nearly 200 kilos for above\-average specimens. Some particularly large krogan weigh in at about 800 pounds (\~362 kilos), estimated independently by themselves and by non\-krogan observers. Biotic individuals are rare, though those who do possess the talent typically have strong abilities. The most amazing physiological feature of krogan biology is the multiple instances of major organs. These secondary (and where applicable, tertiary) systems are capable of serving as back\-ups in the event of damage to the primary biological structures. They have, for example, two hearts, four lungs, and four testicles. This reflects in their slang, where they often speak about a "quad" where a human would use the words "balls" or "pair". Instead of a traditional nervous system, Krogan have a second circulatory system using a neuroconductive fluid, meaning they are almost impossible to paralyze, as any lost fluid is replaced over time similar to blood. Krogan bleed a yellow or orange fluid when shot, which may be this fluid or actual blood. Aside from redundant systems, the legendary krogan "blood rage" adds to the race's reputation for being notoriously difficult to kill or incapacitate in normal combat scenarios. In this state, krogan become totally unresponsive to pain and will fight to the death regardless of injury level, with the side effect of reducing their capacity for logic and self\-control. Sheer physical hardiness means an individual krogan can expect to live for centuries. Krogan can live for well over a thousand years, as evidenced by Warlord Okeer, a veteran of the Krogan Rebellions who died (of decidedly unnatural causes) well over a thousand years after the Rebellions ended. Nakmor Drack is another example of their long life\-spans, a 1,400\-year\-old veteran of the Krogan Rebellions who joined the Andromeda Initiative to voyage to the Heleus Cluster. Some elder krogan such as Drack can develop benign boney growths as facial exostosis which may resemble a spikey beard. Despite their natural propensity for toughness, krogan do have physical weaknesses. According to Zaeed Massani, if one lodges a knife at a certain spot near the frontal plate on a krogan's head, the plate can be ripped off. It is apparently the one thing krogan do fear.

evidence.text:
Thessia was the asari homeworld, the second planet of the Parnitha System in the Athena Nebula, and the core of the largest economy in the Milky Way. It has been called the "crown jewel of the galaxy," the "apex of democracy," and the "beating heart of galactic love." Its republics had a remarkably low incidence of war, disease, violent crime and famine, supported by wealthy colonies and Thessia's vast element zero reserves, which were large enough to affect the price of eezo galaxy-wide. Traces of element zero in the water and soil were so common that most native life adapted to it, making the world home to many biotically active and eezo-resistant species. Travel to Thessia was strictly controlled, though smuggling persisted.

Rather than a single government, Thessia was host to varying republics, each with a formidable military, and had long been free of internal or external wars. The asari were renowned for cultural and political dominance and excelled at diplomacy, holding a strong presence in Citadel politics. This unfocused political structure left the Thessians unprepared for the Reaper invasion of 2186, which eliminated the communications infrastructure underpinning asari e-democracy and left millions without power, water or food, a deliberate Reaper strategy since husks alone struggled to subdue a population full of biotics. The planet became the setting of the mission Priority: Thessia.

Cultural details include a distinctive fashion sense with non-asari patrons such as Edan Had'dah; food and drink served with small amounts of element zero, prompting a separate visitors' menu, though the drink elasa could be consumed by asari and non-asari alike; and native plants such as the common irssal, a honey-smelling blossom whose seeds were carried by colonists toward the Andromeda galaxy. Thessia lay on the Illium–Thessia shipping lane. The name is adapted from Thessaly, whose "witches" Roman writers said could draw down the moon.

evidence.text:
The turians were a militaristic, disciplined species from the planet Palaven in the Trebia system, and the third race to join the Citadel Council. Their civilization spanned fifteen thousand years and was known to the Protheans, who considered them primitive. The first turian ship to use a relay was the THV Ravuna. Around the time the asari and salarians formed the Council, the turians were fighting the Unification War among their far-flung colonies, run by local chieftains who had drifted from the Hierarchy; colonists adopted facial markings to distinguish themselves, a practice that survived into the modern era. The Hierarchy stayed neutral until fewer than a dozen factions remained, then intervened and forced reunification.

During the Krogan Rebellions the Council made first contact with the turians and enlisted their war machine against the krogan. The turians suffered devastating counterattacks, losing three worlds to asteroid bombardment and fighting the bloodiest battle in their history at Digeris, before deploying the salarian-developed genophage, subduing most krogan by 800 CE. In gratitude they received a full Council seat by 900 CE and took over the peacekeeping role left by the krogan. In 2157 a turian fleet fired on human explorers activating an uncharted relay, triggering the Relay 314 Incident (First Contact War); turians besieged and briefly occupied Shanxi before the Council imposed peace and ordered reparations, leaving lasting mistrust. During the 2186 Reaper War the Reapers destroyed Taetrus and assaulted Palaven and Menae; a joint turian-krogan counterattack achieved the "Miracle at Palaven" by smuggling warp bombs aboard Reaper ships, before Primarch Victus withdrew the fleet to join the assault on Earth.

Biologically, turians stood over six feet tall with avian, raptor-like features, taloned two-fingered hands, mandibles, and a reflective metallic carapace containing thulium that shielded them from Palaven's high solar radiation. They were viviparous, had dark blue blood, distinctively flanging voices, and were built on dextro-amino acids, sharing that trait only with quarians; levo food was at best non-nutritious and at worst fatally allergenic. Females lacked the swept-back cranial crests of males. Their lifespan was comparable to a human's.

evidence.text:
Priority: Earth was the final mission of Mass Effect 3 and the conclusion of Commander Shepard's trilogy. It was acquired after Priority: Cerberus Headquarters; from that point Sol was the only reachable system, and merely traveling there triggered the mission with no way to back out. Allied fleets assaulted the Reapers above Earth while Hammer, the ground force, tried to land troops near the Citadel transport beam.

The mission had two main stages. First, Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" so Hammer could land; the team fought through streets and a ruined house full of Cannibals, Marauders, and Brutes to a crashed assault team, recovered two M-920 Cain shots to destroy the cannon, held off a Banshee (named "Morinth" if that character survived Mass Effect 2) and endless Cannibals, and were extracted, reuniting with Anderson and meeting Major Coats. At the Forward Operating Base, Shepard held final conversations with surviving squadmates, allies, and leaders (Victus, Wrex or Wreav, Kirrahe, and others depending on prior choices) before Anderson gave the battle plan: a frontal armored assault on the conduit past a Reaper Destroyer.

The second stage advanced through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles were coordinated with EDI on the Normandy to destroy the Destroyer while the team fought Brutes, Banshees, and a Harvester and dodged the Reaper's beam. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final push, but Harbinger descended on the conduit and annihilated the ground forces. In the Extended Cut, squadmates survived or died based on Effective Military Strength (below 4200 EMS in Legendary Edition they died). A wounded, solitary Shepard fought through Husks and a Marauder with an infinite-clip pistol to reach the beam.

On the reconfigured Citadel, Shepard reunited by comm with Anderson and found him held hostage by a transformed Illusive Man, who could now control both of them. The confrontation's outcome hinged on the final choice, with full Paragon/Renegade options requiring Paragon/Renegade choices at every prior meeting with the Illusive Man. Paragon made him realize he was indoctrinated and shoot himself; Renegade interrupts let Shepard kill him. Shepard then opened the Citadel arms to let the Crucible dock. The Catalyst appeared and offered Destruction, Control, or Synthesis (Refusal was also possible), with availability and galactic damage set by EMS. Every activated ending crippled the Normandy, and its crew's survival, the epilogue scenes, and the placing of Shepard's name plaque above Anderson's on the memorial wall all depended on EMS and prior choices. After the credits a Stargazer told a child tales of "the Shepard."

evidence.text: Shepard alerts Hackett and Anderson to their discovery of the Catalyst's identity and location. With no alternative, Hackett and Shepard order the forces they have gathered to the Sol system with the intention of taking Earth back from the Reapers. Hackett and Anderson brief Shepard on the three\-fold plan of battle: 'Sword' Fleet will engage the Reapers in space, while 'Hammer' ground forces will land in London. When Shepard queries why London is their landing zone, Anderson explains that the Reapers have established a teleportation beam between the city and the Citadel to transport dead and living humans to the station, presumably to be harvested. The plan is for Hammer ground forces to fight their way through the city to the beam, and get as many people as possible on board the Citadel and find a way to open the station's arms. Once this is done, Hackett will signal 'Shield' Fleet, which will remain outside the Sol system protecting the Crucible, to pass through the Charon relay and clear a path for the Crucible to dock with the Citadel. All forces deploy for the Sol System and a brutal space battle ensues between the fleets Shepard has gathered and the Reapers in orbit around Earth. The Normandy breaks off from the battle and descends to the planet. Shepard and several other squads have been ordered to take out Reaper Destroyers planet\-side, fitted with anti\-aircraft Hades Cannons that threaten Hammer's landing. After eliminating the destroyers, Shepard and their squad are extracted by Anderson and local resistance forces, who convey them back to their forward base. At the same time, Hammer troops begin landing en masse in preparation for the assault on the Citadel beam. When the bulk of surviving Hammer forces have landed and deployed, Anderson briefs Shepard and the other team leaders that they must fight their way through the city to the beam, though they will need to take out another Reaper Destroyer blocking their path en route. Using Thanix missile batteries and EDI's help to overcome interference in the guidance systems from the Citadel beam, the Destroyer is brought down, but by that time, Hammer's forces have suffered heavy casualties, Reaper forces are gaining ground and to make matters worse, Hackett warns that several Sovereign\-class Reapers, including Harbinger, have broken away from the space battle and are descending to Earth. By the time the remnants of Hammer reach the Citadel beam's immediate vicinity, Harbinger has already deployed to protect it. Hammer attacks, but Harbinger annihilates them; countless soldiers are killed and Shepard's squad is severely injured (possibly killed, depending on how prepared the galaxy's forces are). With its stealth technology, the Normandy is able to move in and carry Shepard's squad to safety, if they're still alive, without Harbinger noticing. Almost immediately after the ship's departure however the Commander is hit by Harbinger and critically injured. Believing itself victorious, Harbinger retreats back to the space battle, not noticing Shepard managing to get back to their feet and stagger into the beam. Upon arriving aboard the Citadel, Shepard is contacted by Anderson, who followed them up but was somehow separated. The two find themselves dumped in similar\-looking tunnels; keepers prowl about and there are human corpses dumped everywhere. Staggering to what looks like a control room, Shepard and Anderson are ambushed by the Illusive Man, the skin of his face and neck rotted and riddled with Reaper tech. These "upgrades" allow him to take control of their motor functions, even forcing Shepard to shoot Anderson. The Illusive Man again asserts the necessity of controlling the Reapers and that the Crucible will grant him that power, but it is clear to Shepard and Anderson that he is deeply indoctrinated. Shepard can try to convince the Illusive Man, like Saren before him, to fight his indoctrination, prompting the Illusive Man to commit suicide to escape the Reapers' control; otherwise the Commander is able to briefly shake off the Illusive Man's influence and shoot him. In this case, the Illusive Man turns to the view of Earth and with his dying breath laments that Shepard could not see humanity and Earth the way he sees them: perfect. With the Illusive Man dealt with, Shepard opens the arms of the Citadel and Hackett orders Shield Fleet, along with the Crucible to move in. The Crucible successfully docks with the Citadel, but nothing happens. At this point, Shepard and Anderson, if he is still alive, sit together and look at the vast blue planet beyond. Anderson tells Shepard that he is proud of them and it has been an honor to fight at his protegé's side. After this final conversation, Anderson dies from his injuries and Shepard passes out from blood loss.

evidence.text: - The Krogan Warlord Sentinel is the only krogan with health regeneration and 1250 base shields. The health regeneration is considerable but still won't be sufficient to withstand a concentrated attack on you on higher difficulties. - Because of the huge size of the krogan and inability to use cover, maps with lots of high cover and walls are favorable for the Warlord as they make the use of "soft cover" (i.e. standing behind terrain without clinging to it) more easily. Maps with small "sections", or areas that are separated by walls and cover, are good as they make it easier for the Warlord to get within melee range of enemies packed together by the map layout. Conversely, wide open areas are less desirable. - Krogan Charge is replaced with a hammer attack that uses a charge based on the current hammer power. If no charges are present, then it will simply strike with the hammer. - Your current amount of charges is visible on the hammer as holographic rings (Electric Hammer) or biotic charges on the back of the hammer (Biotic Hammer). Keep an eye on it, to make sure you recharge it before using it. - Unlike the Krogan Charge of other krogan characters, the hammer blow will lock onto closer enemies even if they're moving. Geth Bombers are an exception to this; if they increase their height or zoom past the player, the hammer will strike nothing. - Running while executing the heavy melee will still allow the Krogan Warlord to do the Krogan Charge. The Krogan Warlord is unique in that its Krogan Charge deals damage in a small arc in front of the character. - When a Hammer Power is equipped, power damage bonuses increase the damage added by the power to the hammer, in addition to any melee bonuses. When the hammer is uncharged, only melee upgrades affect damage output. - It is possible to use the heavy melee to cancel the animation of any hammer power when being activated (charging), allowing the Warlord to quickly unleash his charged hammer blow. - It is also possible to fire and even reload weapons that have a charged shot function (e.g. the Graal Spike Thrower) during the hammer power activation period, as long as a shot began charging beforehand. The hammer power activation can also be used for reload cancelling like most other powers. - Pressing the melee button again after the Krogan Headbutt allows a second and third hit using the Battle Hammer; the final strike with the Hammer will consume any Hammer Power equipped. - The Warlord has the second highest hit\-stun resistance in the game, following the Geth Juggernaut Soldier, and it constantly regenerates health, making it one of the best characters to tank with. - Despite its size and low mobility, the Warlord is not immune to sync kills. To effectively fight enemies with sync kill attacks one should stand just out of reach, activate whatever hammer powers will be applied, and utilize conventional weapons until the target initiates one of its other attacks. This opening should easily be long enough to deliver a heavy melee and back off before the subject can recover. - Standing above or below (NOT beside) an enemy on a ramp will make it difficult for it to sync kill you. - The Warlord spends a great deal of its time in melee attacks, making many weapons less useful. Many players, therefore, choose an armament that deals great damage in a very short period of time. Most shotguns naturally fit this role, but the Executioner Pistol proves remarkably effective at slinging exactly one shot between melee hits while also dealing effective damage at moderate range. The Pistol Melee Stunner together with the Pistol Power Magnifier is a viable alternative to the Shotgun Omni\-Blade for a Warlord who makes frequent use of Tech Armor detonation. - Melee mods are multiplicative with respect to the damage bonuses that they grant, while power mods are additive. While power mods add a minor bonus to Tech Armor, and the hammer powers, a melee mod adds a significant bonus to both hammer powers as well as melee attacks. This makes melee mods a much better choice than power mods. Because hammer powers add damage to the regular melee attack, increasing melee damage indirectly increases hammer power damage by a much larger amount than a power mod could. - The Warlord also spends a lot of time roaring after melee kills (see the main Rage page for details), especially if the Rank 6 Pure Rage evolution of Warlord Rage is taken. The best ways to cancel the roar animations are to hold down sprint after melee kills or to use heavy melee attacks repeatedly.

evidence.text: You're now in the Forward Operating Base (FOB), where Hammer will assemble before making a move on the conduit. Your squad and Anderson head into the FOB, leaving you with Coats for a short conversation where he tells you of how inspirational you will be to your comrades in arms before leaving to rejoin his unit. Head down the ladder onto the street. Explore the base to engage in final conversations with your squadmates. The number of squadmates can range from as few as three (if Garrus or Tali did not survive the events of Mass Effect 2, or if Tali did not live through the battle on Rannoch, and if the Virmire Survivor died during the Cerberus coup attempt or was not allowed back on the Normandy in its aftermath) to as many as seven (if all possible squad members survived and Javik was recruited). Through the door on the street is the Communications Tech Officer. You may ask him to speak to Cortez and any previous squadmates from Mass Effect 2 (provided they are alive) via a vidcomm terminal in the building behind the Virmire Survivor's location. There is a datapad across from the street from the Communications Tech officer in between a few trucks. It reads about asking volunteers from the fire patrol. You can listen to interesting updates on the mission by a group of soldiers on the street. Head up a ramp to the left of the door (it blends into the rubble). You will run into Primarch Victus and Garrus (if alive). Head through the door to the walkway. Make sure that you are ready to leave the area, as you cannot go back through the door. A cutscene occurs after which you'll find yourself in a turret\-gun minigame which ends after a set amount of time. On the other side of the walkway you'll find Liara, two medkits, and a radio conversation if you want to stop and listen. If you speak to Liara, her initial response varies depending on how you performed on the turret: if you allowed **more than seven Husks** to reach the buildings, her response will be that there were heavier losses and some of the wounded "won't make it". Otherwise, she will say they haven't brought in many additional wounded. There is also a datapad just through the door to the right. Through the next door is Javik and the current leader of the krogan (Urdnot Wrex/Urdnot Wreav) giving 4 different speeches. If you sabotaged the genophage and Wrex was the krogan leader, Kirrahe or another STG officer ("Colonel Vaykom") if he is dead will be found at the same spot as the Urdnot Clan Leader, giving a speech to salarian ground forces instead. Through the final door, you will find EDI, Tali, a medkit, and Anderson, who is conferring with Major Coats. If the geth destroyed the quarians at Rannoch, a Geth Prime will be present instead of Tali. If the quarians were victorious at Rannoch but Tali died in Mass Effect 2, Admiral Raan will take her place. Once you've spoken to everyone you want to, talk to Anderson. He will tell you the percentage of Hammer team that has reported in. The battle plan is simple: a direct, frontal assault on the conduit with tanks and supporting infantry, including your team, in the hopes of getting forces through the transport beam to the Citadel. Of course, resistance is bound to be heavy, and there's one other problem: a Reaper Destroyer is parked near the conduit. After you tell Anderson you're ready to proceed with the attack and make an inspiring or grimly determined speech to your teammates, you'll have a last chance to pick your final squad and make adjustments. You'll be facing the same enemy types as before, just at a higher percentage and density of the various boss types.

evidence.text:
The Krogan Warlord Sentinel was a playable class in Mass Effect 3 multiplayer, presented in-fiction as an elder krogan statesman who held no regard for combat honor, resorting to hostage-taking and genocide, and who carried a battle hammer while his maturity granted unsurpassed regeneration. It had 1250 shields and 1000 health, and the powers Tech Armor, Biotic Hammer, Electrical Hammer and Warlord Rage. Its melee was a Krogan Headbutt that could chain into two hammer swings, the last imbued with the equipped hammer power; a sprinting Krogan Charge dealt damage in a small arc. It could not take cover, vault, dodge, or perform grabs, and moved slower than other krogan classes, but could not be grabbed by Husks or Abominations and had the second-highest hit-stun resistance in the game after the Geth Juggernaut.

It was the only krogan class with both health regeneration and 1250 base shields, making it one of the best tanking characters. The Krogan Charge was replaced by a hammer strike consuming holographic charges based on the current hammer power, which locked onto moving enemies. Melee mods (multiplicative) were far better than power mods since hammer powers added damage to melee attacks; a Biotic Hammer with the Shotgun Omni-Blade V could deal roughly 7,000 to health and shields, 8,000 to barriers and 10,000 to armor. Electrical Hammer's Chill Effect set up devastating Biotic Hammer follow-ups. Extensive player notes covered every faction, stressing that its slow heavy melee left it exposed to sync-kill enemies such as Phantoms, Atlases, Scions, Praetorians, Banshees and Brutes, best handled by striking first or staying just out of reach. It uniquely never used the "For Tuchanka!" voice line common to other krogan classes.
