evidence.text:
Major Coats was a British Systems Alliance soldier stationed on Earth during the Reaper invasion, serving under the command of Admiral Anderson. Before Hammer's final assault, Coats spent three days holed up inside the Big Ben clock tower in London, firing at anything that moved.

During the final battle on Earth, Coats provided covering fire while Commander Shepard was extracted by a UT-47 Kodiak Drop Shuttle. Admiral Anderson later ordered him to coordinate the artillery strikes that supported Shepard's team as it advanced toward the Citadel beam. After Shepard was hit by Harbinger during the run on the beam, Coats was heard over the radio ordering all surviving soldiers to fall back from the attack.

The aftermath depended on Shepard's choices. If Shepard activated the Crucible, Coats was seen helping rebuild London alongside Gabriella Daniels and Kenneth Donnelly, provided the engineering pair had also survived the war. If Shepard had not brought most of the galaxy's forces into the final battle, Coats was instead shown smoking a cigarette amid London's ruins.

Coats first appeared inside Big Ben in the debut trailer for Mass Effect 3 and again in the "Take Earth Back" trailer, and he referenced his time in the tower in dialogue before Hammer's attack. He was voiced by Nick Boulton, who also voiced Reyes Vidal in Mass Effect: Andromeda and the male Hawke in Dragon Age.

evidence.text:
Destroyers were a type of Reaper that appeared during the galaxy-wide Reaper invasion of 2186. Standing roughly 160 meters tall, they were far smaller than Sovereign-class capital ships, which exceeded two kilometers, but they made up the majority of the Reaper fleet. They were believed to be constructed from harvested species not used to build capital ships. Despite their size, Destroyers were formidable: their main gun could destroy a cruiser in seconds, though a cruiser could also bring one down fairly quickly. Their design featured four main legs and five jointed appendages around the "head," with frontal plates that folded aside to expose a powerful beam weapon. They escorted capital ships and destroyed smaller targets such as frigates. On the ground, they unfolded their legs to walk as heavy walkers supporting husks, nearly immune to ground vehicle fire. Being smaller, they were more agile than capital ships and could land directly on larger spacecraft to attack at point-blank range.

Commander Shepard encountered five Destroyers during the Reaper War, four of which were seen destroyed. While escaping Earth aboard the Normandy SR-2 during the initial attack, Shepard witnessed a Destroyer shoot down a shuttle carrying a boy the Commander had met earlier. On Tuchanka, during the mission to disseminate the genophage cure, Shepard summoned the thresher maw Kalros to attack a Destroyer guarding the Shroud; the Reaper was crushed and dragged underground. On Rannoch, while freeing the geth from Reaper control, Shepard discovered that a Destroyer's main weapon firing chamber in its "eye" was vulnerable while charging, and destroyed the Reaper by directing quarian fleet orbital strikes with a handheld laser designator and the Normandy's weapon guidance systems. Before dying, that Destroyer told Shepard the Reapers' cycle must continue or all organic life was doomed, and that the explanation was beyond Shepard's comprehension.

During the battle for Earth, Shepard helped destroy two more Destroyers: one mounting a Hades Cannon was killed with an M-920 Cain to let Hammer forces land in London, and a second guarding the Citadel beam was destroyed when EDI programmed multiple Thanix missile batteries to strike its main weapon, which Shepard activated manually, succeeding on the second attempt. According to BioWare, the Destroyer design was based on a leaf insect nymph, which had also been an early basis for Sovereign's design.

evidence.text:
The Conduit was a device sought by Saren Arterius and Matriarch Benezia during Mass Effect, believed by them to be the key to bringing back the Reapers. Commander Shepard first learned of it from audio files Tali retrieved from one of Saren's geth. Captain David Anderson assumed it was a weapon, while Liara T'Soni, a Prothean expert, knew only fragments suggesting it was linked to the Prothean extinction.

Its true nature was revealed by Vigil, a damaged virtual intelligence on Ilos. The Conduit was a miniature mass relay built by Prothean researchers on Ilos as a prototype during their experiments with relay technology. It functioned as a one-way "back door" onto the Citadel, independent of and unconnected to the rest of the relay network. Its receiving end on the Citadel had been mistaken for a piece of Prothean art, the Relay Monument, and was never removed by the Council; Garrus noted the keepers ignored the statue, and Kaidan reported a low humming from it. The surviving Prothean scientists used the Conduit to reach the Citadel after the Reapers had left, and altered the signal the keepers received from Sovereign that would have opened the Citadel relay to dark space. Because the corridor was one-directional, the researchers were trapped on the station and, as Vigil suggested, left to starve.

Pursuing Saren back to the Citadel, Shepard's team drove the Mako straight into the Conduit seconds before it shut down, dodging the Geth Colossi guarding it, and arrived on the Citadel to launch a counterattack. Living matter could not survive the trip on foot, requiring an enclosed vehicle. Technically the Conduit comprised both the Ilos prototype relay and the Relay Monument, forming the sending and receiving ends of one system. By 2185, in Mass Effect 2, the public had learned some details of the Conduit, and a Presidium Groundskeeper referred to it while recommending Shepard view nearby demael flowers.

evidence.text: *Main article: Sovereign* The first living Reaper to be witnessed by any living intelligent being after the Protheans became extinct was designated Sovereign by the organic races. It is a colossal dreadnought, several times the size of any known vessel – even dwarfing the massive asari flagship, Destiny Ascension. It was first discovered on the edges of geth space in the Perseus Veil by Edan Had'dah's survey teams and studied by Dr. Shu Qian. Saren Arterius, using the doctor's notes stolen sometime in 2165 CE, eventually finds it for himself. At first, it was presumed to be Saren's flagship by those who encountered it; Sovereign did act as transport for the rogue Spectre and his minions. However, Commander Shepard later discovers that Sovereign and its brethren are actually the masterminds behind the Prothean genocide. It acts as the Reapers' vanguard and was originally intended to initiate the next harvest of the galaxy. When Sovereign decided it was time to begin the cycle again, the keepers ignored the order. This greatly complicated matters for Sovereign. In order to unleash its brethren from dark space, it would have to find a way to manually activate the relay from inside the Citadel. While Reapers are undoubtedly beings of terrible power and ferocity, a single Reaper would not be able to survive the combined might of the assembled Citadel races in a direct assault. At some point Sovereign became aware of the Conduit and swayed a significant number of geth into worshiping it. It used Saren to comprehend the Conduit's location from Prothean Beacons while putting its geth in a supporting military capacity. Successful in both regards, in 2183 CE the Reaper marshals its forces and launches an all\-out assault on the Citadel while Saren infiltrates the Citadel through the Conduit. Fortunately, Saren is stopped by Commander Shepard and company, and Sovereign is destroyed by the Alliance Fleet, though this would only forestall the Reaper invasion for a few years. Shepard knows the Reaper fleet, though dormant and hibernating, is still out in dark space and vows to find some way to stop them.

evidence.text:
"Race Against Time: Conduit" was the Mass Effect mission that followed "Ilos: Find the Conduit," into which the earlier "Race Against Time: Sovereign" journal entry was renamed. Vigil had revealed that the Conduit was not a weapon but a miniature mass relay serving as a back door onto the Citadel, itself an enormous mass relay. Saren Arterius intended to use the Conduit to reach the Citadel, unlock the station for Sovereign, and trigger a Reaper invasion that would destroy all organic life in the galaxy.

The mission was a linear drive in the Mako out of Vigil's chamber and down a path now cleared of the forcefields that had blocked it earlier. Shepard's squadmates remarked that even the Protheans, with all their power and knowledge, had fallen for the Reapers' traps, and vowed not to share their fate. Geth Rocket Troopers guarded the entrance to a long trench run, which was defended by numerous geth including Rocket Troopers, Troopers, a Shock Trooper, and a Geth Colossus, followed by further groups of Rocket Troopers. There were no item pickups during the driving sections, and the game would not allow Shepard to enter the aqueducts or the Conduit itself without the Mako; entering the Conduit on foot meant instant death.

At the end of the aqueduct the Mako halted at a ledge overlooking the distant Conduit, and a lengthy cutscene showed the Battle of the Citadel beginning: Sovereign and its geth allies arrived through the mass relay and fired a devastating broadside on the Citadel Fleet, the Citadel forces failed to seal the station's arms, and the commander of the Destiny Ascension ordered the Council evacuated. On the Presidium, a geth threw aside the body of an asari as Saren and his minions took the elevator toward the Council Chambers. Regaining control, Shepard had only 40 seconds to reach the Conduit while dodging four Geth Colossi, then drove into the Conduit, which automatically transported the Mako to the Citadel. The mission led directly into "Race Against Time: Final Battle."

The Shroud is determined to be the best solution for distributing the cure; however, a Destroyer\-class Reaper is found to have seized control of the tower for the purpose of poisoning Tuchanka's atmosphere. Shepard and their squad dodge the Destroyer's beam to reach two maw hammers, which draw Kalros to the site. Kalros attacks the Destroyer. The Reaper smashes Kalros into the Shroud, damaging it, but Kalros drags the Reaper underground, effectively incapacitating it and allowing Shepard to proceed. Afterwards Shepard reaches the Shroud where Mordin/Wiks is done finalizing the cure, although a temperature malfunction in the control room is preventing its viable distribution. Due to countermeasures put in place by the STG, remote bypass is impossible and the salarian scientist must access the controls manually in order to ensure the temperature range is acceptable. Regardless of whether the cure is distributed, the Shroud is eventually destroyed as it explodes.

evidence.text:
Banshees were synthetic-organic creatures in Mass Effect 3, derived from asari and mutated by Reaper technology. The page described them as frighteningly intelligent advanced pressure units usually found leading a Reaper strike force. The Reapers created them specifically from asari with active or latent predispositions to becoming Ardat-Yakshi, a rare neurological condition that enhances biotic power while causing the immediate death of anyone the asari mates with. Emaciated and lumbering as though in constant pain, Banshees were nonetheless durable, able to hurl lethal balls of energy, create shockwaves as they regenerated, spawn their own warp field, and seemingly teleport during combat. When a Banshee died, its Ardat-Yakshi genetics twisted against it, causing a biotic implosion to prevent capture.

Offensively, while glowing, Banshees covered ground rapidly by teleporting in a series of biotic "hops" that could pass through thin cover or walls, and could grab a foe and impale them for an instant kill or perform a heavy two-armed downward swipe. When not glowing they could crouch and spring up with a damaging Nova-like biotic blast with a mild draining effect, and could throw slow but tracking Warp-like biotic projectiles that shattered shields and inflicted damage over time. Defensively they had highly durable barriers and armor, with depleted barriers regenerating quickly; dealing enough armor damage forced a Banshee to stop glowing and teleporting for a time. When not glowing they could raise a hand to create a field negating almost all offensive powers. A Banshee's head was a weak spot taking 40% bonus damage from headshot weapons.

The tactics section advised treating Banshees as a threat that forced players out of position, sometimes leaving them alone to kill other enemies first, and detailed how the impale sync-kill could be interrupted by staggering damage, killing the Banshee first, or (in multiplayer) the victim being downed by other attacks first. It noted class-specific approaches for Vanguards using Biotic Charge and Nova, and for krogan and batarian characters able to survive the biotic blast without staggering. If Morinth was spared in 2185, she would appear as a Banshee during the assault on Earth, behaving no differently from any other and having to be killed. The page also noted an intact Banshee corpse could be found near Falere in the Ardat-Yakshi Monastery despite the codex claim that Banshee bodies were destroyed on death.

evidence.text:
Husks were synthetic-organic "zombies" created from the bodies of organic beings. Victims, living or dead, were impaled on mechanical spikes that Alliance marines nicknamed "dragon's teeth," which over time converted the body's organs, skin and water into cybernetic materials, turned the blood into a sickly green fluid, and made the body generate an electrical charge. When approached, the spikes released the husks, which charged and unleashed a powerful electrical blast that disabled shields and dealt heavy damage. Fully converted husks retained none of their former personality.

In Mass Effect: Evolution, the Arca Monolith on Shanxi during the First Contact War transformed those who touched it into synthetic thralls; General Desolas Arterius sought to build an army of "meta-turians," while mercenary Jack Harper, only partially exposed, kept his mind but gained altered eyes and the ability to sense the artifact and understand alien languages. Saren Arterius ordered an orbital strike on Temple Palaven, destroying Desolas and the meta-turians. In Mass Effect, husks were encountered from Eden Prime onward wherever humans fought the geth, who used dragon's teeth from Sovereign; Cerberus studied husks for a super-soldier program and exposed a pioneer team on Chasca, and Saren kept husks at his Virmire facility. Sovereign's possession of Saren produced a husk-like creature, suggesting dragon's teeth were Reaper technology; a cache was also found buried on Trebin.

By Mass Effect 2, husks were known to be of Reaper origin. The Collectors deployed husks plus advanced variants: Abominations (explode on contact), Scions (three husks fused, long-range cannons), and Praetorians (thirty husks fused). Dragon's teeth found aboard a derelict Reaper showed the variants had been used at least 37 million years ago, while a Reaper artifact in the Minos Wasteland on Aequitas created husks with an energy orb rather than spikes. Mass Effect: Invasion introduced Cerberus study of husk-like Adjutants at Avernus Station, which escaped and attacked Omega, infecting organics to make more Adjutants. In Mass Effect 3, Reaper victims deemed inadequate for DNA processing were converted into husks; Cerberus's Sanctuary logs on Horizon revealed the transforming nano-machines "ride" on adrenaline molecules and that each husk also serves as a transmitter node for Reaper signals. Reaper husk types included the Banshee (from asari Ardat-Yakshi), Brute (krogan/turian), Cannibal (batarian), Harvester, Marauder (turian), Ravager (rachni) and Swarmer. Activating the Crucible obliterated husks (Destroy), made them flee (Control), or made them docile (Synthesis).

evidence.text:
Lesuss was the first planet of the Mesana System in the Milky Way's Nimbus Cluster, a garden world just outside the comfort zone of its asari population: its gravity was slightly too high, its diseases too virulent, and its soil too poor for growing food. Although it had been settled long ago, its night side showed little light pollution, and the asari government was uncharacteristically silent about it. It lay far from regularly traveled trade routes and was inhabited only by a small asari colony.

The world's main feature was a monastery housing a large population of asari with active or latent Ardat-Yakshi genes, a disorder that killed anyone who mated with the afflicted asari. Some colonists had exiled themselves voluntarily, but many were sent to Lesuss by their families to protect society from their deadly potential. The monastery emphasized individual sacrifice for the good of the community. Latent Ardat-Yakshi, and active sufferers who demonstrated they could control their condition, could be offered a chance to reintegrate into asari society after sufficient time on Lesuss, while active Ardat-Yakshi whose psychological profiles showed capacity for neither empathy nor reeducation were confined to the monastery for life.

During the Reaper War, Asari High Command lost contact with several commando squads sent to Lesuss, prompting Commander Shepard to investigate. The monastery, home to Samara's daughters Falere and Rila, had been attacked by Reaper forces converting its residents into banshees. Lesuss featured in the missions Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery and Citadel: Asari Widow.

evidence.page: Reaper Classes and Sizes (Part 1) — Origin, Purpose, and Ground Forces
evidence.text:
Part 1 of a hand-corrected survey of Reaper types, covering what the Reapers are, their origin, the logic of the harvest, and their ground forces and small constructs. The Reapers were described as gigantic biomechanical machines partly built from living beings, resembling space squids or cuttlefish and ranging in size from a large building to a mountain. Each Reaper housed the fused minds of billions of individuals from a harvested species inside a machine body.

Their origin was traced to roughly a billion years ago, when a race called the Leviathans ruled the galaxy and built a super-intelligent AI to solve the recurring conflict between organic life and the synthetic machines organics create. The AI concluded that permanent control of all life, including the Leviathans, was the only solution. It turned on its makers, wiped out most of them, and used their bodies and minds to build the first Reaper, later known as Harbinger. The process was repeated on other species once they reached a threshold of advancement, producing more Reapers over millions of years.

The harvest was presented as the Reapers' method of preservation: they let civilizations rise using the Citadel and mass relays, which the Reapers secretly built, then returned every 50,000 years to destroy advanced civilizations while preserving their minds inside new Reapers, a form of immortality by the Reapers' reckoning.

The page then catalogs Reaper ground troops and small constructs: husks (bodies converted on dragon's-teeth spikes into cybernetic zombies, the most common troops); cannibals (mutated batarians that consume corpses to grow armor); harvesters (30-to-40-foot flying gunships and transports); marauders (transformed turians acting as battlefield leaders); brutes (turian-krogan hybrids); ravagers (mutated rachni used as living artillery); banshees (corrupted asari with powerful biotics); the Oculus (a fast flying drone used by Reapers and Collectors); and swarmers (tiny, numerous drones).

evidence.text: Along with her guides Janiri and Lucen, Athame is credited for helping to bring enlightenment to the ancient asari, with Janiri teaching them agricultural practices (including the seasons), Lucen teaching them about the stars, and Athame teaching them mathematics and medicine. The ancient asari also believed that Athame protected their homeworld Thessia from attacks by other, jealous gods. The Temple of Athame on Thessia still stands as a reminder of the influence that Athame worship had on asari culture. The temple displays various relics attributed to Athame, including murals, busts of Janiri and Lucen, Athame's sword and shield, and fragments of the Athame Codex, an ancient text that explains how asari learned mathematics and agriculture. Other relics not kept at the temple include the Rings of Alune, which were worn by an asari who was believed to have been taught medicine by Athame herself. As an homage to the goddess, three of the planets in the Parnitha system, the asari's home system, are named for Athame, Janiri, and Lucen. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |
